honestLabel.v1: Side-effect-aware peek: RabbitMQ counts every return of a message, and this plan shows what each step does to it.

W-BROKER-UNVERIFIED.v1: This broker build is not one the registry has verified ({{verification}}). Caps are the conservative defaults, and the effects shown are derived from the code and documentation, not confirmed by a lab run.

W-DLX-UNVERIFIED.v1: The tool could not establish every queue that dead-letters into this one ({{reasons}}). A message that died for exceeding another queue's delivery limit may arrive here with a count above this queue's limit, and RabbitMQ would then drop or dead-letter it on any return, including a peek. The limit is treated as unknown: the guard uses the estimate {{estimate}}.

W-LIMIT-UNKNOWN.v1: The delivery limit of this queue could not be read. The guard uses the estimate {{estimate}}, the lowest limit seen, so more messages count as at risk. Raising the limit is not offered.

W-SEMANTICS-GAP.v1: The registry has no entry for {{cells}}. This plan uses the effects of the nearest conservative entry instead.

INVALID_REQUEST.v1: The request or the preflight is not valid.

GATE.v1: Peeking is switched off for this broker.

STREAM_QUEUE.v1: This is a stream. Streams are read by offset, never with basic.get; use the stream browser.

EXCLUSIVE.v1: This exclusive queue belongs to another connection; RabbitMQ does not allow reading it.

UNVERIFIED_BROKER.v1: This broker build is not verified, so only a person may plan a peek.

NO_QUORUM.v1: The quorum queue has no quorum or its health could not be checked, so it is not peeked.

SAC_ACTIVE.v1: A single active consumer is connected. RabbitMQ refuses basic.get on this quorum queue, and a peek would have to take over from it.

SEMANTICS_GAP.v1: The registry has no entry for this broker and queue, and only a person may plan a peek on a conservative substitute.

LIMIT_MINUS1_313.v1: On RabbitMQ 3.13 a delivery limit of -1 drops a message on its first return, so this queue cannot be peeked.

OVERLIMIT_DLQ.v1: This queue receives dead-lettered messages whose count may be above its own delivery limit; RabbitMQ would drop or dead-letter them on any return, including a peek. Set delivery-limit to -1 on this queue first.

BUDGET_TOO_SMALL.v1: The hold time or the byte cap leaves no room for one message.

METHOD_UNAVAILABLE.v1: The requested way of reading is not available for this queue.

NO_SAFE_DISPOSITION.v1: No safe way to handle a message that a return would drop is available for this run.

RESCUE_PREFLIGHT_FAILED.v1: The quarantine queue cannot be used right now.

count-invalid.v1: The count must be a positive whole number.

max-bytes-invalid.v1: The byte limit must be a positive whole number.

preflight-number-invalid.v1: A number from the preflight is not usable.

raise-limit-value-invalid.v1: The new limit is not allowed for this queue.

typed-consent-mismatch.v1: The typed confirmation does not match the queue name.

gate-disabled.v1: The broker profile switches this feature off.

exclusive-owned-by-other.v1: The queue is exclusive to another connection.

unverified-broker.v1: The broker build is not verified.

quorum-unhealthy.v1: The quorum queue is not known to be healthy.

sac-active-consumer.v1: A single active consumer is connected.

semantics-gap.v1: The registry has no entry for this case.

limit-minus1-destructive.v1: A limit of -1 drops a message on its first return on this version.

dlx-sources-over-limit.v1: A dead-letter source can send messages above this queue's limit.

dlx-source-unbounded.v1: A dead-letter source has no limit, so its messages can arrive with any count.

rtt-invalid.v1: The measured round trip is not usable.

rtt-exceeds-target.v1: One round trip takes longer than the hold target.

hold-hard-abort-too-small.v1: The time limits leave no hold time.

avg-message-exceeds-bytes.v1: An average message is larger than the byte cap.

amqp10-not-available.v1: The AMQP 1.0 path is not available here.

sac-consumer-path-unavailable.v1: The consumer path for a single active consumer queue is not available here.

http-limit-finite.v1: The HTTP fallback is not offered for a queue with a delivery limit.

http-limit-unknown.v1: The HTTP fallback is not offered when the delivery limit is unknown.

http-era-not-strict.v1: The HTTP fallback is not offered on this version.

http-not-provably-non-dlx.v1: The HTTP fallback needs proof that no queue dead-letters into this one.

http-held-death-unchecked.v1: The HTTP fallback needs the death history of held messages to be checked.

no-safe-disposition.v1: Neither a quarantine nor a limit raise is possible.

let-broker-handle-non-human.v1: Only a person may let the broker handle a message.

raise-limit-not-admin.v1: Only an administrator may raise the limit.

raise-limit-capped.v1: An argument or an operator policy fixes the limit.

raise-limit-protected-name.v1: The policy name belongs to another tool or provider.

raise-limit-unknown-limit.v1: The limit cannot be raised while it is unknown.

raise-limit-stale.v1: The preflight is too old for an unattended run.

no-rescue.v1: The quarantine queue was not checked.

rescue-queue-not-ready.v1: The quarantine queue is not ready.

rescue-overflow-unsafe.v1: The quarantine queue could drop messages when it is full.

rescue-permission.v1: The user may not write to the quarantine queue.

rescue-publish-blocked.v1: Publishing is blocked on the broker.

rescue-stale.v1: The quarantine check is too old for an unattended run.
